concepts.name: Shard
concepts.text: 1 MB/s (1,000 rec/s) write, 2 MB/s shared read; MD5 partition key routes records and keeps order per shard.

concepts.name: Capacity Modes
concepts.text: On-demand scales auto (pay/GB) for spiky load; provisioned bills shard-hours for steady traffic.

concepts.name: Enhanced Fan-Out
concepts.text: Dedicated 2 MB/s per shard per consumer pushed over HTTP/2 (~70 ms) instead of shared 2 MB/s pull.

concepts.name: Retention & Replay
concepts.text: 24 h default (up to 365 days); consumers replay from TRIM_HORIZON, AT_TIMESTAMP, or a sequence number.

rows: custom real-time processing, multiple consumers, replay

dedicated 2 MB/s per shard per consumer
unpredictable traffic, no capacity planning wanted
steady, well-known throughput at lowest cost

diagram.heading: Kinesis Data Streams fan-in and fan-out

items.label: Produce
items.text: PutRecords (<=500), KPL (batch/aggregate/retry), or Agent write <=1 MB records with a partition key.

items.label: Shard & Retain
items.text: MD5 hash of the partition key picks a shard; Kinesis assigns a sequence number and retains 24 h-365 days.

items.label: Consume & Replay
items.text: Shared pull or EFO HTTP/2 push feeds consumers; replay via TRIM_HORIZON, LATEST, sequence, or AT_TIMESTAMP.

table.heading: Key Quotas, Modes & Limits
rows: Shared by all consumers; ~200 ms+ latency
KPL aggregates small records (+ slight latency)
Enables replay; archive to S3 via Firehose

tips: KDS does not write directly to S3: use a consumer such as Firehose, Lambda, or a KCL app.
Ordering is guaranteed only within a shard (same partition key), never globally across the stream.
Rising IteratorAgeMilliseconds means consumers lag: scale consumers (shards, Lambda parallelization, EFO).
KCL keeps shard leases and checkpoints in DynamoDB; throttling on that table can stall consumers.
